name: Berkshire Hathaway
description: Berkshire Hathaway is a holding company that owns dozens of wholly-owned operating businesses and a large stock portfolio, run on an unusually decentralized basis. Greg Abel became CEO on January 1, 2026, succeeding Warren Buffett; Abel is responsible for major capital allocation. Profit comes from four places: insurance (GEICO, a commercial primary group and reinsurance), which earns underwriting profit and lets Berkshire invest the premium float; the BNSF railroad and Berkshire Hathaway Energy (regulated utilities and pipelines); a large group of manufacturing, service and retailing businesses (Precision Castparts, Lubrizol, Clayton Homes, McLane, Pilot and others); and gains and dividends on an equity portfolio concentrated in a few stocks. Berkshire also holds a very large cash and Treasury bill pile ($210.3B at June 30, 2026) that earns interest inside insurance investment income. Reported net earnings swing widely because unrealized stock gains and losses run through profit (2025: $30.7B of investment gains).

businessLines.name: Insurance - underwriting (GEICO, BH Primary, BH Reinsurance)
businessLines.how: Customers pay premiums up front for coverage that pays out later; Berkshire keeps underwriting profit when premiums exceed claims and costs. The customer money held before claims are paid (float) is invested, reported separately as investment income.
businessLines.description: GEICO (private passenger auto), Berkshire Hathaway Primary Group (mostly commercial lines) and Berkshire Hathaway Reinsurance Group (excess-of-loss, quota-share, facultative).

revenue.note: Premiums earned: GEICO $44,481M, BH Primary $18,713M, BHRG $25,708M (10-K Note 26)

businessLines.marketShare: GEICO 11.56% (2025, US private passenger auto insurance (GEICO))

businessLines.name: Insurance - investment income
businessLines.how: Interest on Treasury bills and cash plus dividends on stocks held by the insurance companies; falls when short-term rates fall or cash is spent on acquisitions.
businessLines.description: Interest and dividends earned on the insurance float and on Berkshire's cash and Treasury bills.

businessLines.name: BNSF (railroad)
businessLines.how: Freight rates charged per car or unit hauled (coal, grain, intermodal containers, chemicals); revenue per car slipped 0.5% in 2025 while cost cuts lifted profit.
businessLines.description: BNSF Railway, one of the largest freight rail systems in North America.

businessLines.name: Berkshire Hathaway Energy (BHE)
businessLines.how: Regulators set rates that let utilities recover costs and earn a return on the assets they build; pipelines charge fees for moving gas; wind production tax credits reduce the tax bill.
businessLines.description: Regulated electric and gas utilities, interstate natural gas pipelines, power generation and a real estate brokerage.

operatingProfit.label: after-tax earnings attributable to Berkshire, FY2025 (FY2024 $3,730M; FY2023 $2,331M)

businessLines.name: Manufacturing, service and retailing (incl. McLane and Pilot)
businessLines.how: Ordinary product and service sales: jet engine castings, lubricant additives, manufactured homes, wholesale food distribution, truck-stop fuel, aircraft shares. Each subsidiary is run separately and sends spare cash to headquarters.
businessLines.description: Precision Castparts, Lubrizol, Clayton Homes, Marmon and many more; service businesses such as NetJets and FlightSafety; retailers and auto dealers; plus McLane and Pilot (separate segments in Note 26, combined in Berkshire's earnings table).
